en: I perpetually prostrate before the Jina, the Sugata, the Lion of the Śākyas, whose body and complexion are like refined gold, as praised by the nine planets.
The palm of his hand is adorned with the excellent wheel, and he removes the sins of gods, asuras, and humans. || 1 ||
I pay homage to the Guru, the Lord of Sages, who is graceful, who has eternally conquered the host of Māra through his unshakeable composure,
who brings about the awakening to the ten perfections, who causes the realization of the four noble truths, and who is easily accessible.
I bow to the God who brings benefit to gods and men, the supreme deity worshipped by both humans and immortals;
he who destroys the demons of the six states of existence beginning with the gods, and who removes the fear of old age, death, and other evils. (3)

I bow to him who brought forth the burden of enlightenment that creates happiness, who out of a compassionate disposition bestowed his own bliss upon others, and who, unable to endure the suffering of others, was born in the Śākya clan free from defilements and undisturbed by agitation. (4)
I bow to him who, for the welfare of the world, abandoned his home and his father along with his beloved wife;
surrounded by Kaṇṭhaka, Chandaka, and Devadatta, he joyfully departed for the solitary forest.

I bow to him who caused the hosts of great seers dwelling in the penance groves to be filled with wonder— those who were devoted to the four sublime Brahma-abodes and solely dedicated to the vow of asceticism through the recollection of the Sugata.
I bow to the Vajradhara who rests upon an excellent seat of fine grass at the root of the great tree;
he who wields the weapon of the strength of a hundred koṭis of flowers, and is surrounded by a hundred Tathāgata sons. (7)
I bow to the five hundred Mallika merchants who performed the very act of protection;
they offered five vessels of nectar presented by the merchants and partook of the auspicious meal of milk-rice. || 8 ||
I bow to the one who turned the excellent Wheel of Dharma in the Deer Park at the seat of the fourfold assembly;
he is surrounded by Brahmā, Śakra, and the worlds of gods and asuras, his beautiful body illuminating all directions with great splendor.
Indeed, that person who recites this hymn of praise to the Sugata composed by the Guru will never have fear of planetary afflictions or diseases; he shall go to the excellent city of liberation. (10)
The hymn of praise to Śrī Śākyasiṃha, composed [for the purpose of averting] the influence of the nine grahas beginning with Āditya, is completed.
